text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 0.24% today, continuing a two-week rally that's gained 13.2% overall. The broader energy sector has been volatile but supported by two opposing forces: oil prices remain elevated (U.S. crude at $101.91/barrel, Brent around $110), but news on October 19th that the Trump administration may suspend duties on Russian energy and seek sanctions relief sent crude sliding as traders bet on more Russian oil entering global markets. That relief news likely capped gains today even as refineries run at 93.5% utilization — near-full capacity suggests strong refining margins that benefit Marathon.

The two-week gain reflects the earlier spike when Iran's Hormuz attacks pushed Brent above $110, which temporarily supported both crude prices and refining spreads. However, today's muted move suggests the market is settling into a new equilibrium where potential Russian supply relief is offsetting the geopolitical premium from Middle East tension.
